sections.html:
Louisiana calls probate a succession. The goal is a judgment of possession, or in a small estate an affidavit, that shows who now owns what the decedent left. The petition goes to the district court for the parish where the person was domiciled at death. In Orleans Parish that is the Civil District Court.

If the decedent lived outside Louisiana, a succession can be opened in any parish where the person owned immovable property, such as a house. Before you list an inherited home, find out which parish court or clerk of court holds the file.

A small succession covers an estate with a gross value of $200,000 or less at the date of death, when the decedent was domiciled in Louisiana. Code of Civil Procedure art. 3421 sets that limit and a second tier for ancillary successions.

SituationGross value limit
Decedent domiciled in Louisiana$200,000 or less at date of death
Decedent domiciled elsewhere, Louisiana property only (ancillary)$125,000 or less at date of death
Death at least 20 years before the affidavit is signedNo dollar limit

Some older guides still give $125,000 as the general cap. Check the date on anything you read.

sections.h2: Who can use the affidavit instead of going to court?
sections.html:
Article 3431 allows a small succession without opening a court case in three situations. Each is narrower than it first sounds.

  • A Louisiana domiciliary who died without a will.
  • A Louisiana domiciliary who died with a will but left no immovable property in the state, and only if the surviving spouse and every person who would inherit with or without the will agree to waive probate.
  • A non-domiciliary who died without a will, or whose will was probated by court order in another state.

Someone who left a will and owned a Louisiana house falls outside the second item, since a house is immovable property. That estate needs a judicial succession. Paragraph B of the same article also lets a governor-appointed public administrator use the affidavit for small estates with no heir present, after a single advertisement in the official parish journal and no notice of opposition.

sections.h2: What goes in the small succession affidavit
sections.html:
Article 3432 covers the affidavit for an estate with no will. At least two people must swear to it. With a surviving spouse, the spouse signs along with one or more heirs. With no spouse, two heirs sign, or one heir and a second person who knows the facts if there is only one heir.

  • Date of death, domicile, marital status and last residence of the decedent.
  • Each heir's name, last known address and relationship, and the reason any heir did not sign: could not be located after reasonable diligence, or was given 30 days' notice by mail and did not object.
  • A description of the property, labeled community or separate, detailed enough to transfer an immovable.
  • The value of each item and the total at death, each heir's interest, and any usufruct of the surviving spouse.
  • A statement, sworn under penalty of perjury, that each signing heir accepts the succession.

Article 3433, added by Acts 2024, No. 90, covers a non-domiciliary who died with a will. It adds a copy of the will, a certified copy of the other state's probate order, and the legatee's acceptance.

sections.h2: Recording the affidavit to move title to a house
sections.html:
Record the affidavit, or a certified copy, in the conveyance records of the parish where the house sits. Under article 3434 a recorded affidavit is admissible and is prima facie evidence of what it states, including the heirs' relationship to the decedent and their rights in the property.

Banks and others holding the decedent's money or property can rely on a multiple original or certified copy as authority to pay or deliver to the named successors, and they are discharged when they do.

Anyone left out of the affidavit has a window to object. A person who claims to be a successor but was not named has two years from the recording date to assert an interest against a third party who acquired the property for value, or that party's successors. Recording in the right parish matters for another reason: under Civil Code art. 3338 and R.S. 9:2721, an unrecorded instrument has no effect on third persons, and the recorded conveyance must name who pays property tax and give a mailing address for tax notices.

sections.h2: When a court-run succession is needed
sections.html:
You need a judicial succession when the facts fall outside the affidavit rules: a will that must be probated, a house in a testate estate, or an estate above the dollar limit. The aim is a judgment of possession that recognizes the heirs or legatees and puts them in possession.

For an intestate estate with little debt, Code of Civil Procedure arts. 3001 through 3008 allow an ex parte petition for possession by all competent heirs who accept the succession. It usually comes with an Affidavit of Death, Domicile and Heirship under arts. 2821 and 2822, signed by two people with knowledge. Civil Code art. 962 presumes a successor accepts unless there is a written renunciation, which is why filings normally include every successor.

For a testate estate, art. 3031 lets the court put legatees in possession on an ex parte petition from all general and universal legatees. The will must be probated, each legatee must be competent or represented and must accept, and no creditor may have demanded administration. A will must be probated within five years of the judicial opening of the succession under art. 2893, and a succession representative named in the will joins the petition for possession.

sections.h2: Can a succession representative sell the house?
sections.html:
Yes, by private sale if the court approves. Under Code of Civil Procedure art. 3281, the representative files a petition describing the property, the price and conditions, and the reasons for a private sale, and attaches any sale agreement already signed.

The representative may sign the agreement first, as long as it is conditioned on court approval. The petition is due within 30 days after signing.

For heirs in a hurry, this means a buyer can sign a contract while the court paperwork runs. Closing waits on the approval.

sections.h2: Selling an inherited house as an heir
sections.html:
Two problems come up most: proving who owns the house, and paying carrying costs while the paperwork runs.

  • Surviving spouse protections: homestead rights under R.S. 20:1 reach the surviving spouse and minor children of a deceased owner, and the constitutional homestead exemption can continue for a surviving spouse who lives in the home.
  • Property taxes: the tax is a charge on the land, so unpaid balances travel with the house. Redeeming after a tax sale costs the taxes, a 5 percent penalty and 1 percent simple interest per month.

A cash buyer still needs the heirs' ownership documents to close, so finish the affidavit or judgment first if you can. A buyer who purchases as-is also takes over the repair work that stalls many inherited sales.

faqs.q: Do I have to go through court to inherit a house in Louisiana?
faqs.a: Not always. If the decedent lived in Louisiana, died without a will, and left an estate of $200,000 or less, a small succession affidavit under arts. 3431 and 3432 can work. A will plus a house usually means a judicial succession.

faqs.q: How much is a small succession in Louisiana?
faqs.a: $200,000 or less in gross value for a Louisiana domiciliary, and $125,000 or less for an ancillary succession of someone domiciled elsewhere. A death at least 20 years before the affidavit has no dollar limit under art. 3421.

faqs.q: Who signs a small succession affidavit?
faqs.a: At least two people. With a surviving spouse, the spouse signs plus at least one heir. With no spouse, two heirs sign, or one heir and another person who knows the facts.
In the conveyance records of the parish where the house is located, under art. 3434. Banks and others holding the decedent's money may also rely on a certified copy to pay the named heirs.

faqs.q: Can I sell the house before the succession is finished?
faqs.a: A succession representative can sign a private sale agreement before court approval, but the contract is conditioned on the court approving it. The petition must be filed within 30 days of signing.
